A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant proteome response to AMF colonization is a complex process, which is not only dependent on the AMF species but is also affected by the plant genotype and the environmental conditions.
AMF colonization elicits in grapevine roots a complex response involving conserved and species-specific responses.
AMF symbiosis is a strategy for improving plant growth and health in a woody crop species, which is based on the modulation of the plant proteome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteome response to AMF colonising SO4 grapevine is different from that of P-starvation and that the proteome responses are conserved between two Glomus spp. in this plant species.
the AMF-induced proteomic changes in SO4 roots are not only a consequence of the AMF symbiosis but also of the P reprioritisation.
the proteome analysis of grapevine rootstocks colonised by AMF can be a useful approach to identify proteins involved in plant-AMF interactions, which can be further studied in other species.
